f.title: Use an alternative approach only if it satisfies applicable statutes and regulations
f.statement: A firm can use an approach other than the one in this guidance if it satisfies the requirements of the applicable statutes and regulations; to discuss an alternative approach, the firm contacts the FDA office responsible for the guidance as listed on the title page.

f.title: Report blood collection or transfusion fatalities under 21 CFR 606.170(b)
f.statement: Blood collection and transfusion facilities report fatalities related to blood collection or transfusion under 21 CFR 606.170(b); whole blood and blood components are outside the scope of this guidance.
f.clause: I. Introduction (footnote 7)
f.applicability: Whole blood or blood components (excluded from this guidance)

f.title: Submit Fifteen-day reports per 21 CFR 803.12(a) for combination products authorized under a device application
f.statement: As specified in 21 CFR 4.104, combination product applicants are required to submit Fifteen-day reports (as described in 21 CFR 314.80 or 21 CFR 600.80) in accordance with 21 CFR 803.12(a) if the combination product received marketing authorization under a device application. Additional reporting requirements for such products are in 21 CFR part 4, subpart B.
f.clause: I. Introduction (footnote 8)
f.legal_basis: 21 CFR 4.104; 21 CFR 803.12(a); 21 CFR 314.80; 21 CFR 600.80; 21 CFR part 4, subpart B

f.title: Submit lot distribution reports in an electronic format FDA can process, review and archive
f.statement: Lot distribution reports are not considered postmarketing safety reports, but under FDA's final rule (79 FR 33072, June 10, 2014) they are required to be submitted to FDA in an electronic format that the Agency can process, review, and archive (21 CFR 600.81(b)(1)).
f.clause: I. Introduction (footnote 9)
f.applicability: Lot distribution reports (excluded from this guidance)

f.title: Consider electronic submission of HCT/P adverse reaction reports
f.statement: FDA's final rule on electronic safety reporting does not require HCT/P adverse reaction reports to be submitted electronically, but FDA encourages electronic submission of these reports, and this guidance may provide useful information to those interested in submitting them electronically.

f.applicability: HCT/Ps regulated solely under section 361 of the PHS Act

f.title: Submit postmarketing safety reports in an electronic format FDA can process, review and archive
f.statement: Under FDA's June 10, 2014 final rule, persons subject to mandatory postmarketing safety reporting requirements for human drug and biological products must submit safety reports in an electronic format that the Agency can process, review, and archive; the final rule also established 21 CFR 329.100 for electronic submission of reports required by section 760 of the FD&C Act. The compliance date was September 8, 2015.
f.clause: II. Background

rows.actor: Person subject to mandatory postmarketing safety reporting requirements
rows.quote: On June 10, 2014, FDA published a final rule to amend its postmarketing safety reporting regulations for human drug and biological products to require that persons subject to mandatory reporting requirements submit safety reports in an electronic format that the Agency can process, review, and archive. 11 The final rule also established 21 CFR 329.100 to address electronic submission of postmarketing safety reports required by section 760 of the FD&C Act. The compliance date for these requirements was September 8, 2015.
rows.location: II. Background
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves the binding electronic-format requirement and compliance date; taken from Background and the "deadline" is a historical compliance date, not an operational clock.

f.title: Include available and applicable ICSR data elements in the submission
f.statement: The information described by the ICSR data elements listed in the relevant regulations (such as the date of the adverse drug experience, the name of the suspect medical product and the name of the initial reporter) should be included in the ICSR submission if available and applicable to the report.
f.clause: III.A. General Information
f.exceptions: Only if available and applicable to the report

rows.actor: Firm (party with postmarketing safety reporting responsibilities)
rows.quote: An ICSR is made up of data elements, such as the date of an adverse drug experience, the name of a suspect medical product, and the name of the initial reporter. These data elements are listed in the relevant regulations. 17 The information described by the data elements should be included in the ICSR submission if available and applicable to the report.
rows.location: III.A. General Information
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: verified; quote proves statement, level and conditions.

f.title: Make follow-up ICSRs complete, including previously reported and new information
f.statement: A follow-up ICSR, which includes new information about an adverse drug experience previously reported as an initial ICSR, should provide a complete picture of the current understanding of the adverse drug experience rather than only the changes or updates to the initial ICSR; follow-up ICSRs should therefore include the previously reported information along with any new information.
f.clause: III.A. General Information
f.applicability: Follow-up ICSRs

rows.actor: Firm (party with postmarketing safety reporting responsibilities)
rows.quote: A follow-up ICSR includes new information about an adverse drug experience that has been previously reported as an initial ICSR. It should provide a complete picture of the current understanding of an adverse drug experience, rather than providing only the changes and/or updates to an initial ICSR. Accordingly, follow-up ICSRs should include information about an adverse drug experience that has been previously reported along with any new information.
rows.location: III.A. General Information
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: verified; quote proves statement and level.

f.title: Do not resubmit unchanged ICSR attachments with a follow-up ICSR
f.statement: To avoid duplication, ICSR attachments submitted with an initial ICSR (for example literature articles or hospital discharge summaries) should not be resubmitted with a follow-up ICSR unless there are updates to the information.
f.clause: III.A. General Information

f.exceptions: Resubmit when there are updates to the information

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: verified; quote proves statement, level and exception.

f.title: Submit additional device reports for combination products with a device constituent part
f.statement: An applicant whose product is a combination product that contains a device constituent part and was approved under an ANDA, NDA, or BLA must also submit other reports (for example Five-day reports and Malfunction reports), in addition to the postmarketing safety reports associated with the application type, in accordance with 21 CFR part 4, subpart B.
f.clause: III.A. General Information (footnote 18)
f.applicability: Combination products with a device constituent part approved under an ANDA, NDA or BLA

f.title: ICSR report types covered by the electronic ICSR submission procedures
f.statement: The following ICSR report types, required under the cited regulations, are within the guidance's electronic ICSR submission procedures (the same procedures apply to initial and follow-up ICSRs and ICSR attachments): 15-day alert reports required under 21 CFR 314.80(c)(1), 600.80(c)(1) and 310.305(c) (including for prescription drugs compounded by 503B outsourcing facilities); reports for serious, expected, and non-serious adverse drug experiences required under 21 CFR 314.80(c)(2)(ii)(B) and 600.80(c)(2)(ii)(B); serious adverse event reports required under section 760 of the FD&C Act; Five-day reports for combination products with a device constituent part required under 21 CFR 4.102(b)(1), 4.102(c)(1)(i), 803.53 and 803.56; and Malfunction reports for such combination products required under 21 CFR 4.102(b)(1), 4.102(c)(1)(ii), 803.50 and 803.56.
f.clause: III.A. General Information
f.applicability: Initial and follow-up ICSRs and ICSR attachments of the listed report types

f.title: Submit ICSRs and attachments to FAERS via the ESG or the SRP
f.statement: ICSRs and ICSR attachments for human drugs, biological products, and combination products addressed by the guidance are submitted to the FAERS database. FDA provides two options for electronic submission to FAERS: (1) direct submission through the Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG) or (2) submission through the Safety Reporting Portal (SRP), both available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
f.clause: III.B. Options for Electronic Submission of ICSRs: Electronic Submissions Gateway or Safety Reporting Portal

f.title: Include reason, justification, proposed end date and alternative method in waiver requests
f.statement: The waiver request should include the reason for the request and information justifying the waiver (reasons could include, for example, acts of nature, widespread Internet outages, and critical issues with a firm's safety database(s), such as malware attacks). It also should include a proposed end date for the waiver and the proposed alternative reporting method, such as submission on physical media.

dates.title: FDA postmarketing safety reports electronic submission: compliance date
dates.scope: Persons subject to mandatory postmarketing safety reporting for human drugs and nonvaccine biological products (21 CFR 310.305(e), 314.80(g), 314.98, 329.100(c), 600.80(h), 600.81(b)(1), 600.90)
dates.quote: compliance date for these requirements was September 8, 2015.
dates.timing_note: Compliance date of the June 10, 2014 final rule (79 FR 33072) that this guidance implements, as delayed from June 10, 2015 by 80 FR 30151 (May 27, 2015). The guidance itself (April 2022) states no effective date of its own. Held below 90 because the date belongs to the rule.
